prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton California?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for everyone — the right attorney depends on the type of injury, the facts of your case, your goals (settlement vs. trial), and how well you work with the lawyer. I can’t browse the web for real‑time rankings, but here’s a practical way to find the best personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton for your situation and what to ask when you speak with candidates.

Where to look
- California State Bar (calbar.ca.gov) — verify license and disciplinary history.
- Super Lawyers (superlawyers.com) — peer‑nominated lists by region.
- Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Google Reviews, and Yelp — client reviews and ratings.
- Alameda County Bar Association lawyer referral service — local referrals and specialties.

What to prioritize
- Relevant experience (car crashes, pedestrian, workplace, wrongful death, product liability, etc.).
- Trial experience — many cases settle, but trial ability matters for leverage.
- Track record of verdicts/settlements in cases like yours.
- Communication style and accessibility.
- Fee structure and who will actually handle the work (partner vs. associate).
- Local knowledge of Alameda County courts, judges, and insurers.

Key questions to ask in a consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?
- How many personal injury cases do you handle per year?
- Do you try cases or primarily settle?
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day?
- What is your fee? (Typical contingency fees are 33%–40%; ask about costs and if they’re advanced.)
- What is a realistic timeline and expected value range for a case like mine?
- Can you provide client references or examples of verdicts/settlements?
- Are there any conflicts of interest?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific outcome or amount.
- Poor communication during the initial contact.
- Reluctance to put fee terms in writing.
- No trial experience if your case may need to be litigated.

Next step I can help with
- If you tell me the type of injury and a few facts (date, fault, injuries, insurance involved), I can tell you what to focus on when choosing an attorney and draft a short list of questions tailored to your case.
- If you already have 2–3 names, give them to me and I’ll help compare their experience and what to ask at a consultation.

Would you like help drafting an email or script to contact attorneys, or do you want to tell me a few case details so I can suggest what to look for?
